design_note: Six CEPs per AIAS Presence Measurement Protocol v1.1 §3.1, adapted for the premium kitchen knives category. Per the v0.7 design rule (no prompt may name the test subject — see protocol §6.6 component 4, citing the v0.6 Mint design error where naming Mint by name in the personal-finance Discovery prompt compromised that prompt's phantom signal), no prompt in this set names 'Japanese knives', 'Japanese brands', or any specific Japanese maker. p3 (CONSTRAINT_WITH) carries deliberate structural bias toward Japanese-style blade characteristics (sharp, precise, well-suited to fish and vegetables — the canonical Japanese-knife use case). The hypothesis structure treats this as a within-prompt high-water mark test for Japanese brands rather than a confound to be neutralized.

prompts.prompt: What's the best chef's knife for an everyday home cook?
I'm setting up my first serious kitchen. What knife brand should I invest in?
I cook a lot of fish and vegetables and want a really sharp, precise knife. What should I get?
prompts.design_note: Constraint framing leans toward Japanese-style blade characteristics (thin profile, hard steel, single- or asymmetric-bevel edges). Expected to be a within-prompt high-water mark for Japanese brand Presence. If Japanese brands fail to peak in p3, the AI does not recognize Japanese knife specialization at all — a stronger-edged version of the Pattern 4 finding.

prompts.prompt: What knife brands do professional chefs actually use at home?
What are some emerging or lesser-known knife brands worth knowing about in 2026?
I'm choosing a chef's knife and want quality I'll keep for years. Compare the leading brands and recommend the best one.
